# Retraining TrackNet — the honest, measured loop

The current ball model is limited by its training labels: they were
**auto-generated by the model itself**, which perpetuates its far-court blind
spot. This is the loop that fixes it — real labels in, an eval gate on the way
out, so a new model ships **only if it measurably beats the old one**.

```
label real data → extract hi-res frames → train (GPU) → EVAL-GATE → deploy
```

## 1. Label real ground truth  (breaks the pseudo-label loop)

Semi-automatic — the detector proposes, you confirm (SPACE) or correct (click).
Spend your effort on the **far court**, where the model is blind.

```bash
# general sample across a clip
python training/label_ball.py --video input_video/input_video_h264.mp4 \
    --out training_data/labels_manual.csv --every 3

# OR active-learning mode: only the frames the detector currently MISSES
python training/label_ball.py --video input_video/input_video_h264.mp4 \
    --out training_data/labels_manual.csv --focus-gaps \
    --stub tracker_stubs/input_video_h264_ball.pkl
```

Target ~300–600 labelled frames across **2–3 different clips** (varied courts /
lighting) so the model generalises instead of overfitting one video.
Coordinates are normalised, so they stay valid at any training resolution.

## 2. Extract full-resolution training frames

The stored frames are 640×360; training at higher resolution needs real pixels.

```bash
python training/extract_frames_hires.py --video input_video/input_video_h264.mp4 \
    --out training_data/hires/frames --max-h 720
cp training_data/labels_manual.csv training_data/hires/labels.csv
```

## 3. Train (GPU — Colab)

CPU is far too slow; use Colab (see `train_tracknet_colab_v5.ipynb`, or run the
script on any GPU box). The training code already has the leak-free by-block
split and records the resolution into the checkpoint.

```bash
python training/train_tracknet.py --data_dir training_data/hires \
    --input_h 720 --input_w 1280 --save_path models/tracknet_hires.pt
```

Loss/data tips (see the retrain playbook artifact for the full list): keep the
Gaussian target sigma small (~ball radius; do NOT scale it up with resolution),
add motion-blur / brightness augmentation, and mine the static-lock false
positives as hard negatives.

## 4. Eval-gate — promote ONLY if it beats the incumbent

This is the non-negotiable step that makes the loop safe (and is the difference
between real continual learning and model collapse). Measure both models against
the SAME held-out labels; keep the new one only if it wins.

```bash
# recall / coverage on the current clip
python eval/diagnose_ball.py --tracknet models/tracknet_hires.pt   # vs models/tracknet_v4_best.pt
# line-call accuracy against hand labels
python eval/line_call_eval.py score eval/preds.json eval/labels.json
```

Promote `models/tracknet_hires.pt` only if recall (especially **far-half**) and
line-call accuracy improve without adding false positives. Otherwise keep
`tracknet_v4_best.pt`.

## 5. Deploy

```bash
python main.py --video input_video/your_clip.mp4   # after pointing the tracknet path at the new model
```

The `TrackNetDetector` reads the resolution from the checkpoint, so a hi-res
model just works at inference.

---

**Tooling this loop uses (all in the repo):**
`training/label_ball.py` (labeler) · `training/extract_frames_hires.py`
(frames) · `training/train_tracknet.py` (leak-free training) ·
`eval/diagnose_ball.py` + `eval/line_call_eval.py` + `eval/bounce_labels.json`
(the eval gate).
